title: MoEP physical-path Mirror factoring with real active-compute accounting
native_physical_object: native MoEP sparsely routed Attention–FFN blocks, original small GPT2/LLaMA/Gemma controls under BabyLM strict-small protocol
mirror_insertion: short path × layer m on shareable physical block weights while keeping native MoEP routing decisions fixed
logical_multiplicity: many logical specialist module paths from fewer paid physical blocks
hypothesis: Native MoEP path modularity can be retained when logical whole-block specialists are generated by compact m from fewer physical blocks; savings must survive native MoEP layer-level routing and original FFN-only MoE baselines at equal active compute, not merely parameter count.
implementation_steps: First synthetic causal 2-layer d32 sequence task with different ordered operator routes (2 common+2 private rules), source-only teacher rule family, 4 physical blocks and 4/8 logical block roles. Freeze native per-sequence path router (no oracle route peek) and compare native separate MoEP blocks, native tied block+ learned timestep/role embeddings, native low-rank block residual, Mirror Q/m view and Mirror+private rank1. Tests: block-symmetry and causal mask/KV invalidation, correct route discovery, full versus active layer FLOP, one-physical-block serialized inference. For actual MoEP include native GPT2/LLaMA/Gemma BabyLM and Pythia-1B negative scale controls as published; do not infer efficient scaling from synthetic BabyLM. On CPU count block GEMMs; any GPU TTFT claim needs trace-accurate sparse kernel and memory migration.
mandatory_native_controls: native MoEP original whole-block routing, native FFN-only MoE and dense/weight-tied block, same-byte depth embedding or low-rank task block, native pre-gated offload, full independent blocks
measurements: heldout BabyLM NLL/BLiMP or controlled toy compositional CE, exact block-call MAC/FLOPs, actual whole-model disk & GPU HBM high-watermark, TTFT/TPOT, prefetch misses
counterhypothesis: MoEP paper itself warns whole-block MoE may not inherit FFN-MoE scaling efficiency. Mirror may add costly runtime transformations around Attention and destroy cache compatibility.
uncertainty: Router decision entanglement, sequence lengths, unverified native BabyLM checkpoint releases, hardware kernel; per-sequence rather than token as independent unit.

gates.PASS: On >=4/5 fresh heldout composed path worlds NLL within +0.02 nat/token of native MoEP and same-byte FFN-only MoE, total actual bytes <=0.85 native at P95<=1.10, and improves beyond native tied-block role embedding/same-byte LoRA.
gates.FAIL: Whole-block routing costs/invalid cached states dominate, native FFN MoE or ordinary tied block matches and lower active compute, Mirror m expands to full block weight size, natural BabyLM quality degrades.
gates.UNCERTAIN: missing strong native reproduction, real bytes or credible natural heldout quality / intervals

adoption: independent natural >=10 task-world replications; no historical scientific status changed
